### Issue types

| Type | Use it for | Parent |
|---|---|---|

| Task | Small work that is not a deliverable, for example a configuration change or a chore | The Epic of the week |
| Bug | A behavior that does not agree with the acceptance criterion or the design | The Epic of the week in which it is fixed |
| Subtask | One step of a Story, Task or Bug | Story, Task or Bug |

Work that is not done by Friday moves to the Epic of the next week.

### Fields

- **Summary.** Short, in English, in the imperative. A Story that covers acceptance criteria puts their IDs at the end, for example `Pay an order with PayPal (A2-AC-014, A2-AC-015)`.
- **Parent.** Every Story, Task and Bug has the Epic of its week as parent.
- **Description.** Use the template below.
- **Labels.**
  - The release: `R0`, `R0.x`, `RC` or `R1`.
  - The module, for Stories, Tasks and Bugs in one module: `mod-identity`, `mod-commerce`, `mod-subscription`, `mod-commission`, `mod-journey`, `mod-content`, `mod-ai`, `mod-integration` or `mod-kernel` ([architecture section 4](architecture.md#4-modules)). Work across modules, such as CI or planning, has no module label.
  - The scope per module is tracked with the module label, not with the Epic. The project has no Fix Version or Component field at this time.
- **Story point estimate.** The team sets it in sprint planning. Do not set it unless asked.
- **Sprint, Assignee.** Do not set them unless asked.

### Description template

```markdown
## Context
Why this work is necessary. One to three sentences.

## Scope
- What is included.
- What is not included.

## Acceptance criteria
- A2-AC-014: the text of the criterion, or a link to it.

## Sources
- Discovery item IDs, ADRs, design links.
```

A Story also lists its annex items and its inputs (definition of ready, delivery plan section 9). An Epic uses the sections Goal, Exit and Sources.

### Rules for agents

- Read before you write. Search with JQL for an issue that already exists before you create a new one.
- Before you create, change or transition more than one issue, show the list to the user and get approval.
- Do not delete issues. Do not change the status of an issue that another person owns, unless the user asks.
- Write in English.
- Name the issue key in the branch name and in the pull request title, for example branch `AN-123-paypal-checkout` and title `feat: pay an order with PayPal (AN-123)`.
# Event conventions

Source: architecture.md section 4 rule 4, TD-08.

- A module reacts to another module through an event on the bus. It never calls the other module to write. This keeps modules independent and lets the reaction retry.
- **Name:** `<module>.<past-tense-kebab>`, for example `identity.person-registered`.
- **Type:** declare it in the emitting module with `DomainEvent<"<name>", Payload>` and export the type from the module `index.ts`. The payload holds IDs, not copies of personal data.
- **Publish** after the write succeeds: `await bus.publish(event)`.
- **Subscribe** in the reacting module. Put the handlers in `<module>/subscriptions.ts` and export `register<Module>Subscriptions(bus, deps)` from the module `index.ts`. The composition root (`apps/worker/src/index.ts`) calls it.
- The emitting module does not import the reacting module. `pnpm arch` fails on a cycle between modules.
- A handler is idempotent: the same event delivered twice gives the same result.
- List each event in the `AGENTS.md` of the emitting module and of each reacting module.
# Test conventions

Source: delivery plan section 9 (Definition of done), TD-04.

- Write the test first. See it fail. Then write the code.
- Put the test next to the code: `<module>/<name>.test.ts`. vitest.
- **A test that covers an acceptance criterion starts its title with the AC ID**: `it("T3-AC-004: records the consent text version", ...)`. `pnpm trace` reports the coverage.
- Use the in-memory repositories, `InMemoryEventBus` and `fixedClock`. Use `createApp()` from `apps/worker` for a test across modules.
- Fake data only: `@example.test` addresses, invented names.
- Test the edge cases of time in the `Europe/Berlin` calendar (midnight, daylight saving time).

80	**Why a gateway.** T3-D-005 allows ERP access only through the integration module. T2-D-008 asks for one authenticated, encrypted connection. Three reads must be synchronous at the checkout (payment options, the live voucher read, the order history). The integration gateway gives one network identity, one set of ERP credentials and one egress path. The NAV adapter runs only in this unit. See ADR-0006.
81	
82	**Note on T3.** T3 section 3 explains "one application image, one worker image". This design builds one image per web app and one image for the worker and the gateway. T3 allows this change if the acceptance criteria and the T4 values hold (T3 section 3). ADR-0003 records it.
83	
84	## 4. Modules
85	
86	The domain code lives in `packages/core`. It has no dependency on the web framework. Each module owns its PostgreSQL schema and exposes a public API through its `index.ts`. A module never reads another module's tables.
87	
88	| Module         | Owns                                                                                                        | Reads from the ERP (through `integration`)                                     | Emits events                                     |
89	| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
90	| `identity`     | Person, roles with dates, credentials, sessions, staff accounts, consents, preferences, pets, consultations | Customer and advisor master data, assignment                                   | Person registered, consent changed, role started |
91	| `commerce`     | Catalogue view, cart, checkout, payments, voucher redemption, calculators, orders until the hand-off        | Prices, campaigns, vouchers, fees, stock, payment options                      | Order placed, payment captured, order accepted   |
92	| `subscription` | Subscriptions, schedules, due-delivery run, holds, self-service, charge at shipment                         | Shipment report, payment options                                               | Delivery due, delivery charged                   |
93	| `commission`   | Periods, points, levels, runs, statements, comparison, commission settings                                  | Point values, corrections, structure, assignment, invoice status, NAV's result | Run released                                     |
94	| `journey`      | Events, journeys, tasks, leads, messages, advisor e-mails                                                   | Order, invoice and payment events                                              | Task created, message sent                       |
95	| `content`      | Pages, product texts, media and variants, advisor pages, moderation                                         | —                                                                              | Content published                                |
96	| `ai`           | The AI gateway: prompt, limit, record and off switch per function (T3-D-010)                                | —                                                                              | —                                                |
97	| `integration`  | Outbox, copies (`erp_copy` schema), reconciliation, message log, the ERP port client                        | All ERP flows                                                                  | Copy refreshed, message failed                   |
98	| `kernel`       | Rule sets and settings, audit log, pilot switch, feature flags, money, time, IDs                            | —                                                                              | Setting changed                                  |
99	
100	**Rules** (checked in CI, see section 9):
101	
102	1. A module imports another module only through its `index.ts`.
103	2. Only `integration` depends on `packages/erp-port`. Only `apps/integration-gateway` and `apps/worker` load an adapter (`erp-nav`, `erp-fake`, later `erp-bc`).
104	3. `packages/core` does not import the web framework, the HTTP layer or an app.
105	4. Cross-module reactions run through events on the queue, not through direct writes.
106	
107	## 5. Data
108	
109	- **One PostgreSQL database**, one schema per module, plus `erp_copy` for the read copies (T3-D-004, T3-D-007). Drizzle defines the schema and generates the migrations (ADR-0005).
110	- **Migrations are backward compatible**: expand, deploy, then contract. Old and new app versions run at the same time during a blue-green release.
111	- **Every personal data column** carries metadata: purpose, owner, retention. A column without it fails CI (ADR-0011, T3 section 5).
112	- **Every copy row** records its source, its source version and its sync time (T2-D-009).
113	- **Money** is an integer in minor units with a currency. Rounding rules are explicit functions with property tests.
114	- **Time** is stored in UTC. Business rules use the `Europe/Berlin` calendar unless a rule says otherwise (Discovery #102).
115	- **IDs** are UUIDv7 inside the platform. The ERP keys (customer number, advisor number, article number) are separate, indexed columns. Platform order numbers use their own range (T2-O-002).
116	- **The brand field** exists on the entities that a second brand would split (T3-D-013).
117	- **The object store** holds media and its variants, and the migration extracts and reports in the production account. It is reached through a storage port with an S3 adapter, and an Azure Blob adapter if Azure is chosen (ADR-0008).
118

| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `identity`     | Person, roles with dates, credentials, sessions, staff accounts, consents, preferences, pets, consultations | Customer and advisor master data, assignment                                   | Person registered, consent changed, role started |
| `commerce`     | Catalogue view, cart, checkout, payments, voucher redemption, calculators, orders until the hand-off        | Prices, campaigns, vouchers, fees, stock, payment options                      | Order placed, payment captured, order accepted   |
| `subscription` | Subscriptions, schedules, due-delivery run, holds, self-service, charge at shipment                         | Shipment report, payment options                                               | Delivery due, delivery charged                   |
| `commission`   | Periods, points, levels, runs, statements, comparison, commission settings                                  | Point values, corrections, structure, assignment, invoice status, NAV's result | Run released                                     |
| `journey`      | Events, journeys, tasks, leads, messages, advisor e-mails                                                   | Order, invoice and payment events                                              | Task created, message sent                       |
| `content`      | Pages, product texts, media and variants, advisor pages, moderation                                         | —                                                                              | Content published                                |
| `ai`           | The AI gateway: prompt, limit, record and off switch per function (T3-D-010)                                | —                                                                              | —                                                |
| `integration`  | Outbox, copies (`erp_copy` schema), reconciliation, message log, the ERP port client                        | All ERP flows                                                                  | Copy refreshed, message failed                   |
| `kernel`       | Rule sets and settings, audit log, pilot switch, feature flags, money, time, IDs                            | —                                                                              | Setting changed                                  |

**Rules** (checked in CI, see section 9):

1. A module imports another module only through its `index.ts`.
2. Only `integration` depends on `packages/erp-port`. Only `apps/integration-gateway` and `apps/worker` load an adapter (`erp-nav`, `erp-fake`, later `erp-bc`).
3. `packages/core` does not import the web framework, the HTTP layer or an app.
4. Cross-module reactions run through events on the queue, not through direct writes.

## 5. Data

- **One PostgreSQL database**, one schema per module, plus `erp_copy` for the read copies (T3-D-004, T3-D-007). Drizzle defines the schema and generates the migrations (ADR-0005).
- **Migrations are backward compatible**: expand, deploy, then contract. Old and new app versions run at the same time during a blue-green release.
- **Every personal data column** carries metadata: purpose, owner, retention. A column without it fails CI (ADR-0011, T3 section 5).
- **Every copy row** records its source, its source version and its sync time (T2-D-009).
- **Money** is an integer in minor units with a currency. Rounding rules are explicit functions with property tests.
- **Time** is stored in UTC. Business rules use the `Europe/Berlin` calendar unless a rule says otherwise (Discovery #102).
- **IDs** are UUIDv7 inside the platform. The ERP keys (customer number, advisor number, article number) are separate, indexed columns. Platform order numbers use their own range (T2-O-002).
- **The brand field** exists on the entities that a second brand would split (T3-D-013).
- **The object store** holds media and its variants, and the migration extracts and reports in the production account. It is reached through a storage port with an S3 adapter, and an Azure Blob adapter if Azure is chosen (ADR-0008).

After `app.identity.registerPerson(...)` in the app that `createApp()` builds, `app.journey.listTasks(personId)` now shows the welcome call task. `pnpm check` passes. I couldn't commit, though: the permission mode blocked the git commands, so the changes are still uncommitted on `main`.

**What changed**
- **New subscription** in `packages/core/src/journey/subscriptions.ts`: when `identity.person-registered` arrives, journey creates a task with kind `welcome-call`, title `Welcome call`, due on the Berlin date of the registration. It uses the event's own timestamp, so a task handled late still gets the registration date. If the event arrives twice, it doesn't create a second task. `createApp()` in `apps/worker/src/index.ts` turns it on, and it is exported from the journey `index.ts`.
- **Bug fix in `kernel.businessDate`**: it returned the UTC date, not the Berlin date its docs promise (Discovery #102). Someone registering between midnight and 01:00 Berlin time (02:00 in summer) would have had a task due the day before.
- **Tests**: new tests for the subscription; a test through `createApp()` with a registration at 00:30 Berlin time; tests for Berlin midnight in winter and summer and for both clock changes. I saw them fail before writing the code.
- **Docs**: `journey/AGENTS.md` lists the new exports, the event it reacts to and two new rules: one welcome call per person, due on the registration date. `identity/AGENTS.md` notes that journey uses the event.

**Decisions for you**
- **No AC ID**: the discovery baseline has no acceptance criterion for the welcome call, so the new test titles don't start with one. I didn't invent an ID. If there is one, add it to the titles.
- **No Jira key**: none was given. The Jira rules want it in the branch name and the PR title, e.g. `AN-<n>-welcome-call-task` and `feat: create a welcome call task for a new person (AN-<n>)`.
- **No ADR**: I didn't write one. Journey uses an event that identity already publishes, and the module docs already plan for journey to react to other modules' events. If you count adding a new listener as a contract change, it needs an ADR first.

**To finish:**
```
git checkout -b AN-<n>-welcome-call-task
git add -A
git commit -m "feat(journey): create a welcome call task when a person registers" \
  -m "Also fixes kernel.businessDate to use the Europe/Berlin date (Discovery #102)." \
  -m "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
```

If you allow git commands, I can create the branch and commit myself.
